annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States of America (submitted to CCW Group of Governmental Experts)
key_provisions_or_claims: Emerging autonomy technologies can reduce civilian casualties in armed conflict.

Examples: self-destruct/self-deactivation mechanisms, improved awareness of civilians, better collateral damage assessment, automated target identification and engagement, reduced need for immediate self-defense fires.
Cites DoD Directive 3000.09 on autonomy in weapon systems.
States should encourage such innovation rather than stigmatize or ban LAWS technologies.
annotation.summary_en: US working paper to the 2018 CCW Group of Governmental Experts arguing that emerging technologies in lethal autonomous weapon systems can reduce civilian casualties through self-destruct mechanisms, better situational awareness, improved effects assessment, automated targeting and reduced self-defense fires. It urges States to encourage such innovation rather than stigmatize or ban it.
annotation.title_clean: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
annotation.title_en: Humanitarian benefits of emerging technologies in the area of lethal autonomous weapon systems
